title: Rotation Breaks Kibble-Zurek Universality
authors: Shiva Dwivedi, Kenichi Kasamatsu, Adolfo Del Campo, Mithun Thudiyangal
abstract: We show that trap rotation overrides Kibble-Zurek (KZ) universality when a 2D Bose-Einstein condensate forms via a finite-time quench. In stochastic Gross-Pitaevskii simulations, the rotation-induced chiral bias drives the vortex number close to the Feynman-Onsager (FO) value, independent of the quench time. Ramping up rotation with the quench restores the KZ scaling at low frequencies, with vortex numbers below the FO value. The vortices form a disordered lattice that a pinning potential can order into an Abrikosov lattice, even at low rotation. Trap rotation thus offers a control knob for critical dynamics.
summary: This research demonstrates that applying trap rotation to a Bose-Einstein condensate during a quench process breaks the universal scaling predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism. By simulating the system dynamics, the authors show that the macroscopic angular momentum constraint forces the vortex density toward the Feynman-Onsager limit, overriding the expected universal scaling laws.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the presence of trap rotation fundamentally alters the universal scaling laws predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism during the quench process that forms a Bose-Einstein condensate.
main_result: Trap rotation breaks Kibble-Zurek universality, causing the vortex number to be dictated by the Feynman-Onsager limit rather than the quench time scaling. The resulting vortex structure tends toward a vortex-glass phase.
method: The study employs stochastic Gross-Pitaevskii simulations to model the time evolution of the condensate during controlled quenches, comparing results for rotating versus non-rotating systems.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 2D Bose-Einstein condensate undergoing a finite-time quench. The dynamics are governed by the Stochastic Gross-Pitaevskii equation, incorporating terms for trapping potential, rotation ($\Omega$), and stochastic noise.
key_observables: Average vortex number ($\langle n_v angle$), crossover time ($ ar{t}_{eq}$), L-defect density ($ho_{L	ext{-def}}$), and the condensate norm ($ ar{n}(t)$).
important_parameters: Quench time ($	au_Q$), final rotation frequency ($\Omega_f$), and the critical exponents associated with KZ scaling.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the SGPE model and relies on fitting functional forms for the crossover time to extract scaling exponents.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of vortex counts and density profiles, comparing results across different quench protocols (fixed vs. ramping rotation) and showing structural analysis via the structure factor $S(k)$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares quench protocols (Case I: fixed $\Omega$; Case II: ramping $\Omega$) to measure the crossover time ($ ar{t}_{eq}$) and defect density. It first establishes the expected KZ scaling, then demonstrates the deviation caused by the angular momentum constraint imposed by rotation, concluding with structural characterization of the resulting vortex lattice.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how an external, non-critical parameter (rotation) can fundamentally alter the universal scaling laws governing non-equilibrium phase transitions in quantum many-body systems, offering a new control knob for critical dynamics.
